newsitem.title: UK: ACPC lowers Centam coffee crop, world use estimate.
newsitem.headline: ACPC lowers Centam coffee crop, world use estimate.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) said it has lowered its estimate for Central American 1996/97 coffee crop to 15.4 million 60-kg bags from its previous forecast of 15.8 million.
The group also lowered the world coffee consumption estimate to 76 million bags at the most on an annualised basis from 76.5 million previously due to recent retail price rises.
The London-based ACPC also estimated that world coffee availability could fall to 17.91 million bags in the third quarter of 1997 from 18.37 million in the same quarter a year ago.
The ACPC estimates were contained in its latest monthly report, which was distributed to the 14 member states last week and made public on Wednesday.
The group, which is made up of Brazil, Colombia and several Central American, African and Asian producers, accounts for 80 percent of world output.
ACPC kept its estimate for the Brazilian crop unchanged at around 23-24 million bags for 1997/98 and 27 million in 1996/97.

It said continuing high exports, with March shipments at about one million bags, and high cumulative co-operative arrivals suggested that the 1996/97 crop would not too much different from 1995/96 when the crop came in around 28 million.

The ACPC added: "We feel that the higher numbers in circulation and suggested by some of the data may be over-estimated". This was due to the presence of old crop coffee amongst exports and with the addition of government stock sales.
On Colombia, the ACPC repeated the Colombian Coffee Federation's 1996/97 crop estimate of 10.4 million bags but added that there was a potential for a very good flowering for the next main crop.
On the third quarter 1997 outlook, it said the supply prospects for arabicas continued to look tight and vulnerable to disruptions.

"We have assumed 2.3 million bags of exports for Colombia, but a combination of further failures of the crop this year and/or continued concern being expressed over stock quality offered to the exporters could see that threatened," it said.

The ACPC said in the very short-term, recent trade estimates of roaster/origin fixing ratios suggested that roasters had a considerable amount of price-fixing to be done, which would be supportive to New York arabica futures prices.
